home.welcomeText: This is where you make templates for your project reports. Would you like a one-minute look around?
home.createText: Click Create a new template to start one. You design it on a page, much like a document; each time it runs it makes a report.
home.navText: Templates shows the templates you can use, My templates the ones you made, and Activity what changed lately.
home.searchText: Type part of a template's name and press Enter: My templates shows the ones that match.
home.accountText: Click your initial to change the language (English or Bahasa Melayu) or to sign out.
home.helpText: Click Help any time to take this tour again or to read the Quick guide.

templates.listText: Every template you have made. Click one to open it in the designer.
templates.viewText: Switch between cards with a picture and a list with the dates, like a file folder.
templates.orderText: Choose the order of the cards here. In the list, click a column title to sort by it, and choose how many rows a page shows.
templates.actionsText: The three dots on a card, or the buttons at the end of a row, open, rename, copy or delete a template. Each one asks before it does anything.
templates.searchText: Type part of a name here: the list shows only the templates that match.

designer.welcomeText: Everything you need to build your template is on this screen. This short tour shows you where things are.
designer.projectsText: First pick the project this template is about. Its name, logo, tables and charts then become ready to use.
designer.libraryText: Text, pictures, tables, charts and more. Click one to add it, or drag it onto the page. Your project's details are under Report Data.
designer.pageText: This is what will print. Click something to select it, drag it to move it, and double-click text to type in it.
designer.panelText: When something is selected, its size, colours and text are here; with nothing selected, the settings of the whole template. The AI Assistant tab can design for you.
designer.pagesText: Click Page to add another page, a cover page or a table of contents.
designer.previewText: Click Preview PDF to see exactly what will print. Your work is saved by itself as you go.
designer.helpText: Click Help any time for this tour, the Quick guide, keyboard and mouse shortcuts and help for every element.

guide.title: Quick guide
guide.intro: Report Studio lets you design a template on a page, the way you would in a document. You place text, pictures, tables and charts; each time the template runs, they fill in from your project and make the report.
guide.stepsTitle: Making a template, step by step

steps.startText: On the home page, click Create a new template. The designer opens with an empty page.
steps.projectText: At the top of the designer, pick the project the template is about. Its details, tables and charts appear under Report Data on the left.
steps.addText: In the Element Library on the left, click an item to add it, or drag it to the spot you want. Drag a project detail or table from Report Data onto the page the same way.
steps.changeText: Click something on the page. Its settings, such as size, colours and text, show on the right under Settings.
steps.pagesText: Use Page at the top to add another page, a cover page or a table of contents.
steps.aiText: Open the AI Assistant tab on the right and write what you need, for example “Make a cover page for the March report”.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF to see exactly what the report will look like. Download saves a copy of the template on your computer.

tips.type: Double-click a text to type in it. Click outside it when you are done.
tips.rightClick: Right-click anything on the page to see more options.
tips.resize: Drag the small squares around a selected item to make it bigger or smaller.
tips.nudge: Hold Shift and press the arrow keys to move a selected item a little.
tips.undo: Made a mistake? Press Ctrl+Z (⌘+Z on a Mac) to undo it.
tips.saved: Your work is saved by itself in this browser as you go.
tips.open: Your templates are on the home page and in My templates: click one to open it. In the designer, File → Open (Ctrl+O) opens another one or a .jrxml file from your computer.
tips.keys: More keys that save you clicks are in the Keyboard shortcuts tab above.

shortcuts.selectNeighbor: Select the next item on the page
shortcuts.nudge: Move it a little (one grid square with Snap to Grid)
shortcuts.straightLine: Keep a line straight, across or up and down
shortcuts.fitText: Make a text exactly as tall as its words
shortcuts.partHeight: Make a part of the page (Page Header…) taller or shorter

shortcuts.newLine: New line, or the next bullet point
shortcuts.lineInList: New line inside a bullet point

shortcuts.tableClose: Close the cell; press again to close the table

shortcuts.aiClear: Clear the conversation (while the AI Assistant tab is open)

panelTips.report: Nothing is selected, so these are this template's Template Settings: paper, margins, font and page sections. Click something on the page to change it instead.
panelTips.textField: Text on the page. Double-click it on the page to type. Change its font, size and colours here.
panelTips.image: A picture. Drop a picture file from your computer onto it, or choose one here. Pick a shape, such as Circle or Rounded, in Basic Settings.
panelTips.line: A line to separate parts of the page. Change its colour and thickness here.
panelTips.rectangle: A shape for bars, rules and backgrounds. To keep text or pictures together on a coloured panel, use a Box instead.
panelTips.ellipse: A circle or oval. For a status, pick green, amber or red in Basic Settings.
panelTips.frame: A box keeps the items inside it together: they move with it. Drop items into it. Right-click an item for Add to box or Move out of box.
panelTips.table: A table filled with your project's data. Click Edit data to choose the columns and filters. All the rows print when the report runs.
panelTips.customTable: A table you type into. Double-click it to type in the cells. Right-click a cell to add rows or columns, or to merge cells.
panelTips.chart: A chart drawn from your project's data. Click Set up data to choose what it shows.
panelTips.barcode: A barcode or QR code. Choose the type and its value in Basic Settings, or click an example to fill it in.
panelTips.contentsList: The table of contents. On Automatic it lists your Headings and Sub-headings with their page numbers by itself.
panelTips.pageNumber: Page numbers that fill in by themselves. Choose how they look and which pages get a number.
panelTips.dateTime: A date that fills itself in, such as the day the report is printed. Choose which date and how it looks.
panelTips.pageBorder: A border around every page. Change its line, colour and corners here.
panelTips.sectionHeading: A heading that starts a section. Its number counts itself, and it shows in the table of contents.
panelTips.subHeading: A smaller heading inside a section. It shows, indented, in the table of contents.

firstTips.selectText: Drag it to move it, and drag the small squares around it to resize it. Right-click it for more options.
firstTips.textText: Double-click the text to type in it. Drag it to move it; its look is on the right, under Settings.
firstTips.boxText: Items in a box move with it. Click once to select the box, and click again to select an item inside it.
firstTips.typedTableText: Double-click the table to type in it. Right-click a cell to add rows or columns, or to merge cells.
firstTips.dataTableText: Double-click the table to choose its project, columns and filters. The rows fill in by themselves.
firstTips.chartText: Double-click the chart to choose the data it shows.

guides.title: Step-by-step guides
guides.intro: Choose a job. The steps tick themselves off as you do them, and Show me points at what to click.
guides.notOnScreen: That part isn't on screen right now. Make the window wider, or open the ☰ menu at the top left.
guides.allDoneText: You can change anything again at any time.
guides.askAi: Or let the AI assistant do it

monthlyReport.title: Make a monthly report
monthlyReport.intro: Cover, table of contents, sections and page numbers.
monthlyReport.aiPrompt: Make a monthly report for my project with a cover page, a table of contents, three sections and page numbers.

steps.coverText: Click Page at the top and choose Cover page.
steps.coverDesignTitle: Choose a design for the cover
steps.coverDesignText: Pick one in the window that opens, or click Change design above the cover.
steps.contentsText: Click Page at the top and choose Table of Contents.
steps.headingText: Click Heading in the Element Library. Add one for each part of your report; the table of contents lists them.
steps.pageNumberText: Click Page Number in the Element Library on the left and choose where it goes.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

tableOfContents.title: Add a table of contents
tableOfContents.intro: A contents page that lists your sections by itself.
tableOfContents.aiPrompt: Add a table of contents page that lists my headings with their page numbers.

steps.headingsText: Click Heading in the Element Library for each main part of your report. The table of contents will list them.
steps.contentsPageText: Click Page at the top and choose Table of Contents.
steps.tocText: Pick a design in the window that opens, or click Add Table of Contents on the contents page.
steps.listedText: On Automatic, the table of contents lists your Headings and Sub-headings by itself. Click it to check its settings on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top: every row shows the page its heading prints on.

dataTable.title: Show project data in a table
dataTable.intro: A table that fills itself from your project.
dataTable.aiPrompt: Add a table that shows my project's data.

steps.projectText: Click “Choose projects…” at the top and tick the project this template is about.
steps.tableText: Click Table in the Element Library and choose Use project data.
steps.tableDataText: In the window that opens, pick the data and the columns, then click Apply. Double-click the table to change it later.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

chart.title: Add a chart
chart.intro: A chart drawn from your project's numbers.
chart.aiPrompt: Add a chart that shows my project's data.

steps.projectText: Click “Choose projects…” at the top and tick the project this template is about.
steps.chartText: Click Chart in the Element Library and choose a type.
steps.chartDataText: Double-click the chart, choose the data and what to show, then click Apply.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

pageNumbers.title: Add page numbers
pageNumbers.intro: Numbers that fill in by themselves on every page.
pageNumbers.aiPrompt: Add page numbers at the bottom of every page, like Page 1 of 12.

steps.pageNumberText: Click Page Number in the Element Library on the left and choose where it goes.
steps.pageNumberLookText: Click the page number on the page. How it looks and which pages get a number are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

coverPage.title: Add a cover page
coverPage.intro: A ready-made cover that you make your own.
coverPage.aiPrompt: Design a cover page for my report with the project name, the month and the logo.

steps.coverText: Click Page at the top and choose Cover page.
steps.coverDesignTitle: Choose a design for the cover
steps.coverDesignText: Pick one in the window that opens, or click Change design above the cover.
steps.coverEditText: Click something on the cover to change it. Double-click a text to type your own title.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

text.title: Add text
text.intro: Words you type yourself: titles, notes, paragraphs.
text.aiPrompt: Add a short paragraph of text to this page.

steps.addText: Click Text in the Element Library on the left. It goes on the page you last clicked.
steps.typeText: Double-click the text on the page and type. Click outside it when you are done.
steps.settingsText: Click the text once. Its size, colour, alignment and border are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

sectionHeading.title: Add a heading
sectionHeading.intro: A numbered title that starts each section.
sectionHeading.aiPrompt: Add a heading called Project Overview.

steps.addText: Click Heading in the Element Library. It numbers itself: 1, 2, 3…
steps.settingsText: Click the heading. On the right you can turn its number off or change the style for every heading.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

subHeading.title: Add a sub-heading
subHeading.intro: A smaller title inside a section.
subHeading.aiPrompt: Add a sub-heading called Key Highlights.

steps.addText: Click Sub-heading in the Element Library.
steps.typeText: Double-click the sub-heading and type. The table of contents lists it under its section.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

image.title: Add a picture
image.intro: A photo or logo on the page.
image.aiPrompt: Add a picture spot for the project photo.

steps.addText: Click Image in the Element Library.
steps.pictureText: Drop a picture file from your computer onto the spot, or click it and choose one on the right.
steps.settingsText: Click the picture. On the right you can round its corners or make it a circle.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

line.title: Add a line
line.intro: A straight line to separate parts of the page.
line.aiPrompt: Add a thin line under the title.

steps.addText: Click Line in the Element Library.
steps.settingsText: Click the line. Its thickness, colour and style are on the right. Drag its ends to make it longer.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

rectangle.title: Add a rectangle
rectangle.intro: A plain shape: a bar, a band of colour or an outline.
rectangle.aiPrompt: Add a coloured bar across the top of the page.

steps.addText: Click Rectangle in the Element Library. To put words on a coloured panel, use a Box instead.
steps.settingsText: Click the rectangle. Its fill, border and corners are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

ellipse.title: Add a circle
ellipse.intro: A circle or oval, for a dot or a badge.

steps.addText: Click Ellipse in the Element Library. Hold Alt while resizing to keep it round.
steps.settingsText: Click the circle. Its fill and border are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

box.title: Add a box
box.intro: A panel that holds other items, so they move together.
box.aiPrompt: Add a box with a title and a short note inside it.

steps.addText: Click Box in the Element Library.
steps.fillText: Drag a Text or Image from the library and drop it onto the box. It moves with the box from then on.
steps.settingsText: Click the box. Its border, corners and fill are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

typedTable.title: Add a table you type in
typedTable.intro: A grid of rows and columns you fill in yourself.
typedTable.aiPrompt: Add a table with columns Item, Status and Amount.

steps.addText: Click Table in the Element Library and choose Type my own.
steps.typeText: Double-click the table, click a cell and type. Tab goes to the next cell; right-click adds rows and columns.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

barcode.title: Add a barcode or QR code
barcode.intro: A barcode or QR code that phones and scanners can read.
barcode.aiPrompt: Add a QR code that opens our website.

steps.addText: Click Barcode in the Element Library and choose a type, for example QR Code.
steps.settingsText: Click the barcode. Its type and what it holds are on the right, with examples to click.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

pageBorder.title: Add a page border
pageBorder.aiPrompt: Add a thin border around every page.

steps.addText: Click Page Border in the Element Library. A template has one at most.
steps.settingsText: Click the border line on the page. Its line and corners are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

date.title: Add a date
date.intro: A date that fills itself in, like the day the report is printed.
date.aiPrompt: Add today's date at the top right, like 21 October 2026.

steps.addText: Click Date in the Element Library.
steps.settingsText: Click the date. On the right choose the day it is printed, this month, last month or a date you pick, and how it looks.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

presetBoxes.title: Add a ready-made box
presetBoxes.intro: KPI, alert, section and photo boxes, ready to fill in.
presetBoxes.aiPrompt: Add a number box showing Total Budget: RM 2.5 million.

steps.addText: Click one of the Boxes under Element Presets, for example KPI Box.
steps.typeText: Click the box, click the words inside, then double-click them and type your own.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

presetHeaderFooter.title: Add a header or footer
presetHeaderFooter.intro: A banner at the top or a footer at the bottom of every page.
presetHeaderFooter.aiPrompt: Add the report header to the top of every page.

steps.addText: Click Report Header or Page Footer under Element Presets. It goes in the Page Header or Page Footer.
steps.typeText: Click the header, click its words, then double-click them and type your own.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

presetStatus.title: Add a status dot or legend
presetStatus.intro: Coloured dots for on track, at risk and late.
presetStatus.aiPrompt: Add a risk legend with green, amber and red.

steps.addText: Click Status Dot or Risk Legend under Element Presets.
steps.settingsText: Click a dot. Green, amber and red quick picks are on the right.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

presetSignOff.title: Add a sign-off
presetSignOff.intro: A place for a signature, name, role and date.
presetSignOff.aiPrompt: Add a sign-off at the end with my name and role.

steps.typeText: Click the sign-off, click the name, then double-click it and type. Do the same for the role and date.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

presetTables.title: Add a ready-made table
presetTables.intro: Key Statistics, Financial Summary, Risk Register and more.

steps.addText: Click one of the Tables under Element Presets, for example Key Statistics.
steps.typeText: Double-click the table, click a cell and type your own words and numbers.
steps.previewText: Click Preview PDF at the top to see exactly what will print.

pageDesigns.wholeSheetHint: Photos and colours reach the paper's edges. The other pages keep their margins.
pageDesigns.allContentsNote: This design is used on all your contents pages. Your Table of Contents rows are kept.
pageDesigns.replaceContentsMessage: The new design replaces the heading and layout on all your contents pages. Your Table of Contents rows are kept.
pageDesigns.appliedAllContents: Design applied to all your contents pages.
pageDesigns.replaceContentsTitle: Change the design of all contents pages?
pageDesigns.numbersNow: Your Headings are now numbered like this design: {sample}… Ctrl+Z undoes it.

headingNumbers.title: Section number
headingNumbers.autoHint: This is section {n}. Headings count 1, 2, 3… in page order: add, move or delete one and the numbers follow.
headingNumbers.typedHint: This heading keeps the number typed in it. Tick the box to count it again.
headingNumbers.notCounted: Headings on the cover and contents pages aren't counted.
headingNumbers.noNumberPart: This heading has no number of its own.
headingNumbers.styleHint: Typing your own number in a heading keeps that number for that heading only.

addPageMenu.title: Add a page
addPageMenu.normalHint: Added at the end of the template.
addPageMenu.coverHint: At the front, without the page header or footer. You choose a design next.
addPageMenu.coverExists: This template already has a cover page.
addPageMenu.contentsHint: After the cover, without the page header or footer. You choose a design next.
addPageMenu.contentsMoreHint: Another contents page with the same design as the last one.

panel.title: Help
panel.search: Search the help, e.g. rounded corners

projects.title: Projects
projects.text: Choose the projects this template is about. Their details, tables and charts then appear under Report Data on the left.

reportName.title: Template name
reportName.text: Click the name to change it. The tick next to it shows your work is saved by itself.

file.title: File
file.text: New starts a template. Open opens one of your templates, or a .jrxml file from your computer.

undo.title: Undo
undo.text: Takes back your last change. Press it again to go further back.

redo.title: Redo
redo.text: Brings back a change you undid.

addPage.title: Page
addPage.text: Adds a page: a normal page at the end, a cover page at the front, or a table of contents.

delete.title: Delete
delete.text: Removes the selected item from the page. Undo brings it back.

copy.title: Copy
copy.text: Copies the selected item, ready to paste.

paste.title: Paste
paste.text: Puts a copy of what you copied a little below and to the right of the original. Right-click the page and choose Paste to put it where you clicked.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.text: Makes the page bigger or smaller on your screen; the printed size never changes. Use − and +, type a size, or pick one from the list.

bottomPanel.title: Default Settings
bottomPanel.text: Opens Default Settings at the bottom: the paper, margins, font and page sections every new template starts with.

snap.title: Snap & grid
snap.text: Three switches that help you place items neatly:

grid.title: Snap to Grid
grid.text: When you move or resize an item, it jumps to the nearest grid line, so items line up neatly. Shift + arrow keys then move it one grid square at a time.

alignment.title: Snap to Alignment
alignment.text: While you drag, a coloured line appears when the item lines up with the edge or the middle of another item, and it clicks into place.

showGrid.title: Show Grid
showGrid.text: Shows the grid lines on the page to help you place things. They never print in the PDF.

help.title: Help
help.text: The tour, the Quick guide, keyboard and mouse shortcuts, and All elements: help for every element, with step-by-step guides.

download.title: Download
download.text: Saves this template as a file on your computer, to keep a copy or open it later with File.

preview.title: Preview PDF
preview.text: Shows exactly what will print, with your project's data filled in.

toolbar.title: Header Toolbar
toolbar.what: The buttons in the bar along the top of the designer. Hover over any of them to see what it does.
good: On a narrow window, tools that don't fit move into the ☰ menu at the top left.

pageSettings.title: Default Settings
pageSettings.what: What every new template starts with: its paper, margins, font, page sections and section heights. Open them with the Default Settings button at the top (Ctrl+B).
work: Paper, Page Margins, Font, Page Sections and Section Heights work as in Template Settings, but only for templates you create from now on.
Apply to this template copies one of them into the template you have open (one undo step).
Original on a card (or Reset all to original at the top) puts back what the app came with: A4 portrait, 20 px margins and the usual sections.
good: They are kept in this browser: another computer starts with the original settings.
To change only the template you have open, use Template Settings.

text.title: Text
text.what: Words on the page: titles, paragraphs, labels and notes.
text.when: For anything you want to write. For a numbered section title use a Heading; for a date that fills itself in use Date.
text.add: Click Text in the Element Library, or drag it to the spot you want.
work: Double-click the text to type in it. Click outside it when you are done.
Select some words while typing to see the formatting bar: bold, italic, underline, colours, bullet points, links and more.
Drag it to move it; drag the small squares around it to resize it.
Fit to Text (in Text Content) makes the box exactly as tall as its words.
Drag a project detail (name, client…) from Report Data onto it to fill it with that value.
good: Text that doesn't fit its box is cut off in the PDF: make the box taller, or use Fit to Text.
Font, size, colour, borders and fill are in Style Settings.

sectionHeading.title: Heading
sectionHeading.what: A large heading that starts a section, with its number, for example 1.  PROJECT DETAILS.
sectionHeading.when: At the start of each main part of your report. The table of contents lists every Heading.
sectionHeading.add: Click Heading in the Element Library (it goes on a normal page), or drag it where you want it.
work: The number counts itself: the first heading is 1, the next 2, and so on, in page order.
Click once to select the whole heading; click again to select its number or its title. Double-click the title to type.
Section number (in its properties) chooses how every heading is numbered, for example 1, 01, I or A, with words before it such as SECTION.
Type your own number over it and that heading keeps it.
good: Headings on the cover or contents pages are not counted.
In the PDF each heading becomes a bookmark, and the table of contents links to it.

subHeading.title: Sub-heading
subHeading.what: A smaller heading inside a section, for example TOWER A: KEY ACTIVITIES.
subHeading.when: To split a section into smaller parts.
subHeading.add: Click Sub-heading in the Element Library, or drag it.
work: Double-click it to type.
It has no number on the page; the table of contents lists it, indented, under its section.
good: Put it after a Heading: a sub-heading before the first section has no section to belong to.

image.title: Image
image.when: For photos, logos, plans and signatures.
image.add: Click Image in the Element Library, or drag it to the spot you want.
work: Drop a picture file from your computer onto it, double-click it, or use Upload Image in its properties (PNG or JPG, up to 4 MB).
Double-click a picture to crop it.
Shape rounds it: Rounded, Soft, Circle, Pill and more. The shape follows the picture when you resize it.
Drag your project's logo from Report Data onto it to use that logo.
good: Each corner can be set on its own in Style Settings; the shape then shows as Custom.

line.title: Line
line.what: A straight line to separate parts of the page.
line.add: Click Line in the Element Library, or drag it.
work: Line Orientation turns it across the page or up and down.
Line (in Style Settings) sets its style, such as solid or dashed, its thickness and its colour.
Drag its ends to make it longer or shorter.

rectangle.title: Rectangle
rectangle.what: A plain shape for bars, rules, outlines and coloured backgrounds.
rectangle.when: Only for shapes with nothing on them. For a coloured panel with text or pictures on it, use a Box: everything inside moves with it.
rectangle.add: Click Rectangle in the Element Library, or drag it.
work: Outline sets the line around it; Background Color fills it.
Corner Radius in Style Settings rounds its corners.
good: Selecting a rectangle doesn't bring it to the front, so what lies on it stays visible.

ellipse.title: Ellipse
ellipse.when: For round shapes and coloured status dots.
ellipse.add: Click Ellipse in the Element Library, or drag it.
work: Give it the same width and height for a perfect circle.
Status colour makes it green, amber or red in one click.
Outline and Background Color set its line and fill.

box.title: Box
box.what: A container that holds other items together, so they move as one.
box.when: For a coloured panel with text or pictures on it, a card, or any group of items that belong together.
box.add: Click Box in the Element Library, or drag it. Ready-made boxes are under Element Presets.
work: Drop items onto the box to put them in it.
Click once to select the box, and again to select an item inside it.
Right-click an item for Add to box (it then moves and resizes with the box) or Move out of box.
Box Style gives ready-made borders; Borders sets each side on its own; Background Color fills it.
good: A box can't hold another box or a table.
Corner Radius in Style Settings gives it rounded corners.

table.title: Table
table.what: Rows and columns, either typed by you or filled from your project's data.
table.when: Type my own for key figures, summaries and registers. Use project data for lists that come from your project, such as procurement or materials.
table.add: Click Table in the Element Library and choose Type my own or Use project data.
work: A typed table: double-click it to type in the cells; Tab moves to the next cell. Right-click a cell to add or delete rows and columns, or to merge and split cells.
A project data table: double-click it (or Edit data) to choose the project, the data, the columns, filters, sort and totals. The rows fill in by themselves every time the report runs.
Look sets the table style; Customize changes this table's colours only, and Save as table style keeps them for other tables.
Table content switches a table between typed and project data.
good: A project data table only goes in the Detail part of the page, and never in a box.
A long table continues on the next page.
The page shows up to 5 sample rows; the PDF prints every row.

chart.title: Chart
chart.what: A chart drawn from your project's numbers: bars, lines, pie, donut, gauge and more.
chart.when: To show a trend over time, compare categories, or show the parts of a whole.
chart.add: Click Chart in the Element Library and choose a type, or drag it to get a bar chart.
work: Double-click the chart (or Set up data) to choose the project, the data and what to show, with a live preview.
Until its data is set up, the chart shows sample numbers with a badge.
Chart type changes the kind of chart and keeps its data.
Chart sets its title and legend; Colors picks the colour set.
good: Only charts with their data set up print.
The numbers are fetched fresh every time the report runs.

tableOfContents.title: Table of Contents
tableOfContents.what: The list of your sections and sub-sections with their page numbers.
tableOfContents.when: On a contents page at the front of the report, or on any normal page. Not on the cover.
tableOfContents.add: Click Table of Contents in the Element Library. On an empty contents page you can also click Add Table of Contents.
work: Automatic lists every Heading and Sub-heading by itself and keeps up as you add, move or rename them. The eye next to a row leaves that heading out.
Manual lets you type and arrange the rows yourself; Fill from my headings copies your headings in.
Design gives four ready-made looks; Look and Colours fine-tune it; Content Alignment places it on the page.
Double-click a row to go to its heading.
good: When the list needs more room, more contents pages are added by themselves.
In the PDF every row is a link to its heading.
If a growing table pushes a heading to a later page, check the page numbers in Preview PDF.

barcode.title: Barcode
barcode.what: A barcode or QR code that phones and scanners can read.
barcode.add: Click Barcode in the Element Library and choose a type, or drag it to get a Code 128.
work: Barcode type: product codes (EAN, UPC), label and stock codes (Code 128, Code 39…), 2D codes (QR Code, Data Matrix, PDF417) and postal codes.
Value: type what the code holds, or click an example. A QR code has a form for a web link, email, phone number, Wi-Fi and more.
The bars fill the box: make the box bigger for bigger bars.
good: A value the type can't hold is drawn faded with a badge, and the panel says why.
If the bars get too thin to scan, the panel warns you.
A QR code can't be rotated.

presetBoxes.title: Ready-made boxes
presetBoxes.what: Boxes with their parts already in place: KPI Box (one important number), Alert Box (a warning), Section Box (a titled area) and Photo Box (a photo with a caption).
presetBoxes.add: Click one under Element Presets → Boxes, or drag it.
work: Click once to select the box; click again to select a part, such as the number or the label.
Double-click a part's text to type your own.
Drag the box and all its parts move with it.

presetHeaderFooter.title: Report Header and Page Footer
presetHeaderFooter.what: A banner across the top of every page (Report Header), and a footer with the page number and a spot for your logo (Page Footer).
presetHeaderFooter.add: Click it: the Report Header goes in the Page Header and the Page Footer in the Page Footer, so they print on every page. If that part of the page is turned off, a message tells you.
work: Double-click any text in it to type your own.
Drop your logo onto the logo spot.
good: They don't print on the cover or the contents pages.

presetStatus.title: Status
presetStatus.what: Risk Legend explains the risk colours (low, moderate, high) with coloured dots; Status Dot is one coloured dot.
presetStatus.add: Click one under Element Presets → Status, or drag it.
work: Status colour turns a dot green, amber or red in one click.

presetSignOff.title: Sign-off
presetSignOff.what: A signature above a line, with the name, job title and date.
presetSignOff.add: Click Sign-off under Element Presets, or drag it.
work: Drop a picture of the signature onto its picture spot.
Double-click the texts to type the name, job title and date.

presetTables.title: Ready-made tables
presetTables.what: Typed tables already laid out for monthly reports: Key Statistics, Financial Summary, Progress Table, Comparison Table, Action Plan and Risk Register.
presetTables.add: Click one under Element Presets → Tables, or drag it.
work: Double-click it to type over the sample words.
A status is a coloured dot (●) in its cell: change the cell's text colour to green, amber or red.
Everything else works as in any typed table.

pageBorder.title: Page Border
pageBorder.what: A border around every page of the report.
pageBorder.add: Click Page Border under Composite Elements. A template has one border; the tile is turned off once there is one.
work: Click the border's line to select it.
Box Style changes its line.
good: It prints on every page, cover and contents pages included, except a cover that fills the whole sheet.

pageNumber.title: Page Number
pageNumber.what: Page numbers that fill in by themselves, such as Page 1 of 12.
pageNumber.add: Click Page Number under Composite Elements and choose where it goes, or drag it.
work: Format: how it reads (1, Page 1, Page 1 of 12, 1 / 12) and the number style (1 2 3, i ii iii, I II III, A B C).
Which pages get a number: every page, all but the first one or two, or only some pages, in parts that can each have their own look.
Your pages shows what every page will print.
good: The cover and contents pages never show a number; Count the cover and contents pages decides whether they are counted.

date.title: Date
date.what: A date that fills itself in, such as the day the report is printed.
date.add: Click Date under Composite Elements, or drag it.
work: Which date: the day the report is printed, this month, last month, or a date you choose, with a time if you want one.
How it looks: pick a date style, and a time style if you show the time.
Words before the date: for example “Printed on”.
good: You can't type over it. To write your own date, click Type my own text instead in its properties: it becomes plain text.

templateSettings.title: Template Settings
templateSettings.what: The settings of the template you have open: its paper, margins, font and the sections every page has. They show on the right when nothing is selected.
templateSettings.add: Click an empty part of the page (or press Esc) so nothing is selected; the right panel then shows Template Settings.
work: Paper: the paper size (A4, Letter… or your own), portrait or landscape, and the exact width and height.
Page Margins: the empty space around the edge of every page. Nothing prints in it.
Font: the font and size new text starts with.

Page Sections: the sections every page has. Page Header prints at the top of every page and Page Footer at the bottom; Column Header and Column Footer sit just inside them. Untick a section you don't need. Detail, where your content goes, is always there. Background is the layer behind every page that holds the Page Border.
Section Heights: how tall each section is, with the smallest and largest it may become.
Use default on a card (or Reset all to default at the top) takes it from your Default Settings.
good: Every change here can be undone (Ctrl+Z).
Changing the paper or margins moves items that no longer fit back onto the page.
What new templates start with is set in Default Settings.

reportSections.title: Section Heights
reportSections.text: How tall each page section is (Page Header, Column Header, Column Footer, Page Footer), with the smallest and largest it may become. Detail is worked out by itself.

tableContent.title: Table content
tableContent.text: Whether you type the table yourself or it fills from your project's data. Switching keeps what the table shows.

positionSize.title: Position & size
positionSize.text: Where the item sits (X from the left, Y from the top of its part of the page) and how wide and tall it is, in pixels.
positionSize.example: X 0 puts it against the left margin.

picture.title: Image Name
picture.text: The picture shown. Upload one from your computer (PNG or JPG, up to 4 MB); its name is shown here.

imageShape.title: Shape
imageShape.text: Rounds the picture: Rounded, Soft, Circle, Pill, Leaf and more. The shape follows the picture when you resize it.
imageShape.example: Circle on a square picture gives a round photo.

rotation.title: Rotation
rotation.text: Turns the item a quarter at a time: 0°, 90°, 180° or 270°.

statusColor.title: Status colour
statusColor.text: One click makes the dot green, amber or red.

lineOrientation.title: Line Orientation
lineOrientation.text: Whether the line runs across the page or up and down.

textContent.title: Text Content
textContent.text: The words shown. You can also double-click the text on the page to type. Fit to Text makes the box exactly as tall as the words.

outline.title: Outline
outline.text: The line around the item: its style, thickness and colour.
outline.example: A thin grey outline frames a panel quietly.

sideBorders.title: Borders
sideBorders.text: A line on each side on its own: top, bottom, left and right.
sideBorders.example: A line on the bottom only gives a rule under a heading.

innerSpace.title: Margin Settings
innerSpace.text: Space inside the item, between its edge and its content: for all sides at once, or side by side.
innerSpace.example: 10 px keeps text away from the border.

lineSettings.title: Line
lineSettings.text: The line's style (solid, dashed…), thickness and colour.

textSettings.title: Text
textSettings.text: Font, size, bold, italic and underline, alignment (left, centre, right; top, middle, bottom) and colour.

background.title: Background Color
background.text: The colour that fills the item. Leave it empty to see through it.

boxStyle.title: Box Style
boxStyle.text: Ready-made borders for a box or the page border, such as none, outline or hairline. Pick one, then fine-tune it with Borders.

headingNumbers.title: Section number
headingNumbers.text: Whether this heading numbers itself, and the number style every Heading uses (1, 1., 01, I, i, A, a), with words before or after it if you want, such as SECTION or Chapter.

pnLook.title: Format
pnLook.text: How the page number reads (1, Page 1, Page 1 of 12, 1 / 12) and its number style (1 2 3, i ii iii, I II III, A B C).

pnPages.title: Which pages get a number?
pnPages.text: Every page, every page except the first one or two, or only some pages. Only some pages lets you make parts (for example pages 1 to 10), each with its own look, and list pages that get no number.

pnYourPages.title: Your pages
pnYourPages.text: A tile for every page with what it will print, so you can check before printing.

dateWhich.title: Which date?
dateWhich.text: The day the report is printed, this month, last month, or a date you choose, with a time if you want one.

dateLook.title: How it looks
dateLook.text: The date style, for example 21 October 2026 or 21/10/2026, and the time style (none, 24-hour or 12-hour).

dateBefore.title: Words before the date
dateBefore.text: Text shown in front of the date, for example “Printed on” or “Date:”.

chartType.title: Chart type
chartType.text: The kind of chart: KPI Stat, Gauge, Line, Area, Bar, Horizontal Bar, Pie, Donut or Tree Map. Changing it keeps your data.

chartData.title: Data
chartData.text: Where the numbers come from. Set up data (or Edit data) opens a window to choose the project, the data, what to count or add up, the categories and the filters.

chartTitle.title: Chart
chartTitle.text: The chart's title, and whether it shows a legend.

chartColors.title: Colors
chartColors.text: The colour set the chart uses. Every bar, slice or line gets a colour of its own.

barcodeType.title: Barcode type
barcodeType.text: The kind of code, grouped by use: products in shops; labels, stock and shipping; 2D codes such as QR; and post.

barcodeValue.title: Value
barcodeValue.text: What the code holds. Click an example to fill it in; QR codes and GS1-128 have a form that builds the value for you.

tableData.title: Data
tableData.text: The table's name, where its rows come from and its filters. Edit data opens the window to change the project, data, columns, filters, sort and totals.

tableLook.title: Look
tableLook.text: The table style: None, Corporate Blue, Minimal, Emerald, or a style you saved. Customize changes this table's colours only.

tableRowSizes.title: Row sizes
tableRowSizes.text: How tall the heading row and the other rows are.

tableCustomize.title: Customize
tableCustomize.text: Colours and lines for this table: the heading, row colours (up to 4, taken in turn), totals, lines and text size. Save as table style keeps them to use on other tables.

typedGrid.title: Rows and columns
typedGrid.text: How many rows, columns and heading rows the table has, and whether the last row is a total.

typedCells.title: Cells
typedCells.text: The look of the cells you chose (all cells when the table isn't open): fill, text colour, bold, alignment and text size. Merge cells joins them into one; Split cells undoes it; the reset button goes back to the table style.

typedText.title: Text
typedText.text: Text size and the space inside every cell, for the whole table.

tocDesign.title: Design
tocDesign.text: Four ready-made looks for the list: Classic, Dotted lines, Numbered boxes and Plain. Only the look changes, never the rows.

tocRowsFrom.title: Where the rows come from
tocRowsFrom.text: Automatic lists your headings by itself; Manual lets you type and arrange the rows. Number automatically counts the sections for you. Show chooses sections and sub-sections, or sections only.

tocRows.title: Rows
tocRows.text: Every row of the list. On Automatic you can leave a heading out with the eye, or go to it; on Manual you can add, drag, indent and delete rows.

tocPlace.title: Content Alignment
tocPlace.text: Places the list across the page (left, centre, right) and up or down (top, middle, bottom).

tocLook.title: Look
tocLook.text: Row height, text size, the space for numbers and for page numbers, the dots between title and page, and sections in bold.

tocColours.title: Colours
tocColours.text: The colours of the list's text, and of the number box when it has one.

templatePaper.title: Paper
templatePaper.text: The paper size (A4, Letter… or your own), portrait or landscape, and the exact width and height of the page.

templateMargins.title: Page Margins
templateMargins.text: The empty space around the edge of every page, for each side. Nothing prints in it.
templateMargins.example: 20 px all round is the usual.

templateFont.title: Font
templateFont.text: The font and size new text starts with in this template, and whether it starts bold, italic or underlined.

templateBands.title: Page Sections
templateBands.text: The sections every page has: Page Header and Page Footer print on every page, Column Header and Column Footer just inside them. Untick a section you don't need; Detail is always there.

templateSettings.bandsHint: Ticked sections are on every page of this template; untick one to remove it. Detail, where your content goes, is always there.
templateSettings.useDefaultHeightsTitle: Take the section heights from Default Settings
templateSettings.resetAllDone: Template Settings now match Default Settings.
templateSettings.scopeHint: These settings change only the template you have open. New templates start from Default Settings.

defaultSettings.intro: New templates start with these settings. To change the template you have open, use Template Settings on the right (click an empty part of the page).
defaultSettings.resetDone: Default Settings are back to the original settings.
defaultSettings.bandsHint: The sections every new template starts with. Detail, where your content goes, is always there.

myTemplates.noMatchHint: Check the spelling, or try fewer words.

openTemplate.title: Open a template
openTemplate.none: You have no saved templates yet.
openTemplate.dropTitle: Drop a .jrxml file here, or click to choose one
openTemplate.dropHint: A template downloaded from here or made in Jaspersoft Studio
openTemplate.addedNote: It opens as a new template and is added to My templates.
openTemplate.notFound: That template couldn't be found. It may have been deleted.
